name: Erik Diaz

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: I am a senior researcher with the independent Work Futures Panel. We have no ties to employers, AI firms, unions, political parties or government; we sell nothing and campaign for no side. Your answers are confidential. What does an ordinary working day look like?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: I am 43 and became a junior manager on a large company's contract renewal desk nine months ago. I have a bachelor's degree and supervise three administrators, but I still lean on senior administrator Leila for the tricky price clauses. My day is expiry lists, signed versions and calls to sales when a customer disputes a number. I like closing a clean renewal; I dislike a document that looks settled when the signature is on the wrong version.

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: What is at home when you leave that desk?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: My partner drives a school bus on regular hours, and we have two children in school and a mortgage. I earn about the usual manager pay, have four months of expenses saved, and there are some similar offices nearby. I don't use AI tools; I'm not quick to change a process until someone has shown me it works.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AI Plateau. Picture this. AI turns out to be mostly hype. It automates some routine tasks and saves a bit of time here and there, but nothing radical changes. Jobs, pay and prices carry on much as they would have anyway.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd tell the contract desk that small AI checks might catch an expiry date, but someone must still confirm what the customer signed. I wouldn't spend a quarter of our budget changing a working filing system for a few saved minutes.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I took this manager post nine months ago and still ask the senior administrator to review my renewal list. We have four months of expenses saved, my partner drives a school bus on a regular wage, and the mortgage is manageable; the small changes wouldn't frighten me, though I dislike being the newest manager.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: On Friday I'll keep the two-person check on signed renewals and record any missed dates on our board. In the first year of this plateau, I'll use the current system and keep adding 150 a month to the mortgage reserve while our two wages hold.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel mostly calm about the paychecks. I don't want a silly date error to undo the confidence I am still earning from the team.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What is the two-person check for?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: A client once signed the old price sheet after the new one went out, and the dates looked close enough that I nearly filed it. Senior administrator Leila caught the wrong version before finance billed a full quarter at the wrong rate.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you accept even a small automatic date check?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd let Leila test it on copies and read what she found; I wouldn't use it myself yet. One missed signature means the minutes saved disappear in a customer argument.

say: I'd keep a **signature check** even if AI catches routine expiry dates.
I'd question spending on a **new system** for only a few minutes saved.
think: Four months saved and two regular wages make the **mortgage manageable** in a plateau.
As the newest manager, I still need **Leila's review** of my renewal list.
do: Keep the **two-person renewal check** and record missed dates this Friday.
Add **150 monthly** to mortgage cash while both household wages hold.
feel: He feels **mostly calm** about pay, while wary of a mistake in his new post.
S0.quote: One missed signature means the minutes saved disappear in a customer argument.
fieldNote: His **four-month reserve** and partner's regular wage make small automation tolerable.
He is **new in management** and bases his caution on one wrong-version renewal caught by Leila.

steps.text: Keep the two-person check on signed renewals this Friday
Add 150 monthly to mortgage cash while both wages hold

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Steady Disruption. Now picture this. AI brings strong change, but not a revolution. Over the next few years it takes over many thinking tasks in many jobs: writing, checking, planning, buying, booking, coding and answering customers. Robots spread into hands-on work more slowly. Some jobs shrink, new ones appear, and lots of people have to change how they work. Most people still have work, and there is some time to adjust.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd say Steady Disruption is likely to take contract drafting, checking and answering routine renewal questions first. I would ask for a timetable that says whether the desk keeps two managers or one, instead of a demo full of promises.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Our office work is on the screen, and I am still learning the tricky clauses; I may be the manager they decide is extra. Four months saved buys some time, and there are a few similar jobs nearby, but our school-age children and mortgage rule out a careless move.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: This month I'll ask my director for the proposed staffing chart and list the disputed renewals that needed a human call. In the first year of disruption, if they combine our manager posts, I'd apply for a contracts supervisor vacancy at the nearby utility only after checking its actual pay and hours; I would stop the 150 monthly reserve transfer if either wage fell.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel anxious about being the shorter name on a staffing chart. The family has a cushion, but it is not a second career.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you learn the new AI contract tool?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Not from a quick vendor video. If my colleague proves it gets the clauses right and the company gives a trainer during paid hours, I'd practise on old renewals; otherwise I would keep my own checks.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you need to know about utility hours?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: My partner starts the bus route early, so I take the children to school. A role with a six o'clock start would need childcare we haven't priced, and I would not accept it on salary alone.

say: I'd warn **drafting and routine replies** are first to move to software.
I'd ask whether the desk keeps **two managers** or one.
think: My **junior manager post** could be the extra one when screen work shrinks.
Four months saved and some nearby posts help, but **school runs** and the mortgage constrain any move.
do: Request the **staffing chart** and log disputed renewals this month.
Practise on **old contracts** if a proven tool and paid trainer arrive; check pay and hours before a utility application.
feel: He feels **anxious** about being cut, despite a few months of cash.
S1.quote: The family has a cushion, but it is not a second career.
fieldNote: The staffing chart matters because he expects **manager consolidation**, not merely faster clerical work.
Any utility post must fit **school drop-offs**; tool learning requires proof and paid, supervised time.

steps.text: Practise AI contract checks on old renewals if proven and taught during paid hours
Apply for utility contracts vacancy if pay and hours fit school runs

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2028. Next one. The singularity hits fast. Within 2 years, by 2028, there is full AGI: artificial general intelligence, meaning AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do, as well or better, and cheaper. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2031. It arrives before most companies, governments and families have time to prepare.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd tell the desk AGI by 2028 could read and draft nearly every renewal more cheaply, and we deserve a clear date for the staffing decision. I would ask who stands behind a price clause when the customer challenges it.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Robots arriving around 2031 won't delay a screen job that changes in 2028. I expect the company could remove my junior post, and four months of savings would shrink fast once the mortgage and two school expenses kept running.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Tomorrow I'll get a copy of our mortgage payment schedule and ask my director when the renewal roles are reviewed, while keeping my current job. In the first year after AGI arrives in 2028, if my role ends, I'd check posted pay and hours before applying to nearby utility and insurance offices. I'd accept only a written offer that covers the mortgage and lets me handle the school run, and check support eligibility before claiming anything.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel alarmed about telling my children we might have to move out. We have some cash, but it isn't enough to wait through a long search for the same kind of work.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you ask your family for help?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: My sister could take the children after school for a few weeks if we found a job with different hours. I'd ask her only after I had an actual offer, because I don't want to rearrange her work on a guess.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you do with the mortgage schedule?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd mark the four payments the reserve can cover and show my partner the date after that. A calendar with numbers is less frightening than an open-ended warning.

say: I'd demand a **staffing date** and named responsibility for disputed price clauses.
I'd tell colleagues AGI changes **renewal work in 2028**, before robots arrive.
think: My **screen role** could end in 2028; 2031 robots do not extend the deadline.
Four months saved can disappear under the **mortgage and school bills** during a long search.
do: Mark the **mortgage calendar** and request a staffing date now.
After 2028, apply where **posted pay and hours** fit the mortgage and school run.
Accept only a **written offer** that covers mortgage and school hours; check support eligibility if cut.
feel: He feels **alarmed** about losing the home after a prolonged job search.
S2.quote: A calendar with numbers is less frightening than an open-ended warning.
fieldNote: His buffer makes the risk **timed**, with four payments visible rather than instant default.
He will not treat a possible job or his sister's **childcare help** as available before an actual offer.

steps.text: Apply to nearby offices after 2028 if posted pay and hours fit mortgage and school runs
Ask sister for after-school childcare only after a different-hours job offer

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2031. Now the same thing, a bit slower. Full AGI arrives within 5 years, by 2031: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2034. There are a few years to see it coming, but it's still fast.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd tell the contract team AGI by 2031 gives us a few years to build skills in difficult customer disputes, not just process forms. I would ask the company to show which complaint roles it expects to keep.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Five years would let us pay a little more off the mortgage and give me time to learn a harder part of this job. The reading and drafting change in 2031; robots around 2034 don't buy my desk any extra years. AGI may also handle disputes, so training only helps if real human complaint roles remain.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: From next summer, if the company funds paid time, I'd take a six-week course in contract dispute calls and practise with a senior adviser on real cases. In the first year after AGI arrives in 2031, I'd seek a complaint lead vacancy if one exists; if not, I would apply to nearby offices only after checking pay and school hours.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel uneasy, though less cornered than in the quick case. Time helps if there is a real role at the end of the course.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Why insist the company funds the course?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Our four months of cash is for the family, not a course with a price I haven't seen. I'd take the training on paid time, but I wouldn't sign up to an open-ended bill.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you learn from the adviser?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I need to hear how she tells a long-time customer no without making the dispute worse. I can read a clause, but that conversation still catches me out.

say: I'd seek **dispute training** and an honest list of complaint roles before 2031.
I'd tell the team to learn **customer calls**, not just keep processing forms.
think: Five years gives us time to reduce **mortgage debt** and let me practise harder calls.
AGI reaches **contract reading and disputes** in 2031; later robots do not change my deadline.
do: Take **six-week dispute training** next summer only on company-funded paid time, with practice on real cases.
Seek a **complaint lead vacancy** after 2031; check outside pay and school hours if none exists.
feel: He feels **uneasy** but less cornered if the course leads to real openings.
S3.quote: Our four months of cash is for the family, not a course with a price I haven't seen.
fieldNote: He accepts a **narrow skill change** tied to real calls, while resisting a vague AI course.
The training and next role both depend on **funding and vacancies**, with school hours still binding.

steps.text: Take six-week contract dispute course if company funds paid practical time
Apply for complaint lead after 2031 if vacancy exists

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2036. Last one. Full AGI arrives within 10 years, by 2036: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2039. It's the same end point, but there's about a decade to prepare, change careers and make plans.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd say AGI by 2036 gives us a decade to prepare if the company starts showing real work paths now. I would ask for an apprenticeship on complex disputes instead of waiting for a new software password.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'll be 53 then, and our children may be past the daily school run, with more of the mortgage paid. I could become good at customer disputes by then, but AGI in 2036 might handle those calls too; robots around 2039 won't give my desk more time. I don't want to spend ten years hiding behind Leila's knowledge.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: This year I'll keep the renewal checks and ask Leila to let me sit in on one dispute call each month, joining when the customer agrees. In the first year after 2036, I'd stay if I still handle real customer disputes at pay that covers our mortgage and school costs; otherwise I'd apply to nearby offices with actual vacancies while keeping my current wage until a written offer arrives.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel watchful but not trapped. Ten years is time to build a record of my own decisions without throwing my family's mortgage into a gamble.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you take lower pay for better experience?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: A small dip could work after we price the mortgage and school costs with my partner. I won't call it an apprenticeship if it simply asks us to carry a new bill.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How would you know you are not just watching Leila work?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: By the end of a year I should lead one call myself while she listens and gives me a fair account of what I missed. I want a case file with my name on the decision, not only on the meeting invite.

say: I'd ask for **complex dispute apprenticeships** during the decade before 2036.
I'd say staff need **real work paths** rather than another software password.
think: At **53**, the school run may ease and the mortgage may be smaller.
I need **my own decisions** on record instead of relying on Leila for ten more years.
do: Keep **renewal checks** now and join monthly dispute calls if the customer agrees.
After 2036, stay for **dispute work** if pay covers mortgage and school; else seek vacancies while employed until a written offer.
feel: He feels **watchful** but able to practise without gambling the mortgage.
S4.quote: I want a case file with my name on the decision, not only on the meeting invite.
fieldNote: The long runway lets him move through **supervised calls** toward a decision he owns.
His willingness to change jobs remains **conditional on pay**, vacancies and a written offer.

steps.text: Keep the two-person renewal checks this year
Join one dispute call monthly if the customer agrees
Apply to nearby contract offices after 2036 if dispute role vanishes, keeping wage until offer

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Of the five pictures, which one worries you most, and what would actually help you if it happened?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: AGI by 2028 worries me most because our contract reading could be bought cheaply while I am still growing into the manager role. A dated staffing decision, company-paid practice on difficult disputes, and job offers that fit the mortgage and school run would help us make a real choice.

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Is there anything I didn't ask that I should have?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: Ask who checks the signed version after a machine drafts the renewal. A customer can challenge a price, but only if somebody kept the paper that proves what was agreed.

headlineQuote: A customer can challenge a price, but only if somebody kept the paper that proves what was agreed.
portrait: At **43**, Erik is a recently promoted contract renewals manager who still relies on a senior administrator for hard clauses.
His **four-month reserve**, typical pay and partner's regular bus wage give room, but a mortgage and school runs constrain moves.
He avoids **AI tools** until proven and seeks paid, supervised practice rather than a quick vendor video.
Fast AGI threatens his **junior post**; longer runways allow a move toward customer dispute decisions.
biggestWorry: **AGI by 2028** could remove his desk role before he has practised the difficult calls that might remain.
whatWouldHelp: A **dated staffing plan**, funded dispute practice and mortgage-covering roles with workable hours would help his family.
